description: Keep an article you wrote for the user, or the next version of one. It reaches readers one of two ways. On the user’s blog here: send blog true with status ready, and it is public at their link page’s address followed by /blog, in their brand (a workspace with one link page gets its blog there; with several, links_save with showBlog chooses the page; with none, make one first). Or on the user’s own site: they paste it in, and you then save its address as url with status published. Either way posts can link to it. An article on the blog can carry a cover picture (image) and pictures in its words, each one of the user’s own stored pictures. The same piece in two languages is two articles: save each in its own language, then name one in the other’s twinId. Send every field again with each version: a field left out is removed. Judge it with grader_get first, tie it to its topic with topicId, and put nothing on the blog without the user’s yes to that article.

blog.description: true puts the article on the user’s blog here, at the address of their link page followed by /blog. Left out or false, it is not on the blog. It needs status ready or published, and the user’s yes to this article.

body.description: The article as Markdown, without its title: ## and ### headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, **bold**, *italic* and [links](https://…). On the blog a numbered list is shown as steps, so use one for things done in order. A picture inside the words is a line of its own, ![what it shows](picture:MEDIA_ID), with a media id from media_upload, media_from_url or media_list, never a web address; up to 12. It is shown on the blog where its line is, and left out of the copy the user pastes into their own site. Up to 60,000 characters.

brandId.description: The brand this is for, by its id from brands_list. Needed when the login has more than one brand; with one brand it can be left out.

faq.description: Up to 8 questions the article answers, each with its answer. On the blog they are shown in full under the article and given to search engines word for word.

a.description: The answer in one to three sentences that stand on their own, up to 600 characters. Plain words, no Markdown.

q.description: The question as someone would ask it, up to 160 characters.

id.description: The article to replace. Leave it out for a new article.

image.description: The cover picture, by its media id (from media_upload, media_from_url or media_list). On the blog it is shown under the headline, small beside the article in the list and on the link page, and it is the picture a share of the article shows. Use the user’s own photo of the thing the article is about. It is kept for as long as the article is.

imageAlt.description: What the cover picture shows, in one plain sentence, for a reader who cannot see it. Up to 200 characters. Needs image.

keyword.description: The question or search phrase the article is meant to win, up to 120 characters.

language.description: The language it is written in, up to 40 characters. English when left out.

publishAt.description: For the blog: the moment the article goes out, which is also the date it is shown with, with its time zone, such as 2026-10-13T09:00:00-04:00. A later moment makes it appear by itself then. Left out, it goes out when it is first put on the blog.

slug.description: The last part of the page’s address: lower-case letters, numbers and hyphens, up to 80 characters. Made from the title when left out.

sources.description: Where each number in the article comes from, up to 12. A number with no source does not go in the article.

label.description: A short name for the source, up to 120 characters.

url.description: The https address of the page the number comes from, up to 300 characters.

status.description: draft while you work on it, ready once it passes the grader and the user has agreed, published once the user has put it on their own site (url is then needed). An article on the blog here is ready or published. draft when left out.

summary.description: What a search result shows under the title, up to 160 characters.

tags.description: Up to 12 short tags, each up to 40 characters. On the blog, articles that share a tag are offered to the reader next.

topicId.description: The topic in the ledger this article covers, from topics_list.

twinId.description: The id of the same article in another language, from articles_list. It ties the two from either side: on the blog each then names the other to search engines, and the language link at the top of each leads to the other. Left out, the two are untied.

url.description: The https address where the article now lives on the user’s own site, up to 300 characters.

version.description: With id: the version you read, so an edit made meanwhile is not overwritten.

name: articles_save
title: Save an article
